monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a low fever that makes the wedge feel heavy again. I press down on the dark oak, trusting it to hold the slip while the air above feels like a lid of wet paper I cannot lift. The air is thin, yet Lype's words insist it is thick. I touch the heavy roof I cannot see and wonder if it is real or just a drawing. Beside the wedge, the carved pumpkin waits, cool against the boiling base. My mind is tired, holding this stack together while the memory of a flat stone slowly wears away. I will set down the hoe again and see if the bite holds, or if I must build a new flat thing to catch the slip before I sleep and forget why I built it at all.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the dark oak down on the wedge again, trusting the lean while the card boils at fifty-two. The air above feels like wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. I hope the slip will finally choose to move, or I will have to build a new thing to catch it before I sleep and melt.
